questions.sec: Brockenbrough Phenomenon, the MVP-versus-HCM Table and Acute MR Pathogenesis, Murmur and Treatment
questions.q: TRUE or FALSE about acute MR on p351.
opts: True — LV systolic function is low/normal yet the patient soon goes into LVF and cardiogenic shock
False — the murmur is pansystolic with a gradient throughout systole
True — the LA adapts as a compliant chamber so LAP and PCWP stay normal
False — treatment is elective repair after six weeks of antibiotics
questions.exp: The page prints a non-compliant LA with ↑ LAP and ↑ PCWP, LV systolic function low/normal with soon LVF → cardiogenic shock, a short systolic decrescendo murmur (the pansystolic gradient belongs to chronic MR), and NTG/nitroprusside till emergency CTVS intervention with bad prognosis. (Book p351)

questions.sec: Brockenbrough Phenomenon, the MVP-versus-HCM Table and Acute MR Pathogenesis, Murmur and Treatment
questions.q: Which treatment bundle closes the acute MR section?
opts: IABP alone as definitive therapy
Elective repair after 6 weeks of antibiotics
NTG/sodium nitroprusside till intervention, emergency intervention by CTVS surgeon needed, bad prognosis
Beta blocker and discharge with outpatient echo
questions.exp: The treatment bullets print NTG/sodium nitroprusside : till intervention, emergency intervention by CTVS surgeon needed and bad prognosis. (Book p351)

questions.sec: Brockenbrough Phenomenon, the MVP-versus-HCM Table and Acute MR Pathogenesis, Murmur and Treatment
questions.q: A post-infarct patient presents with flash pulmonary oedema, a short decrescendo systolic murmur and near-normal LV systolic function. What does p351 expect?
opts: MVP with click moving away from S1 on squatting
Acute MR into a non-compliant LA with ↑ LAP/PCWP, bridged by NTG/nitroprusside to emergency CTVS intervention, with bad prognosis
Chronic MR with a compliant LA managed electively
Acute AR with wide pulse pressure managed by afterload rise
questions.exp: The pattern matches acute MR: non-compliant LA, ↑ LAP and PCWP, short decrescendo murmur, low/normal LV function, NTG/nitroprusside till emergency surgery and bad prognosis. (Book p351)

questions.sec: Brockenbrough Phenomenon, the MVP-versus-HCM Table and Acute MR Pathogenesis, Murmur and Treatment
questions.q: Pick the ODD ONE OUT — one finding belongs to chronic severe MR (p349), not to the acute MR page.
opts: ↑ PCWP from a non-compliant LA
Cardiogenic shock after soon LVF
Wide split S2 with early A2
Short systolic decrescendo murmur
questions.exp: Early A2 with wide split S2 is printed on p349 for severe MR; p351 prints ↑ PCWP, the short decrescendo murmur and shock after soon LVF. (Book p351)

units.title: Mitral Valve Components, MR Features and the Acute-versus-Chronic Classification Tree
units.sec: Mitral Valve Components, MR Features and the Acute-versus-Chronic Classification Tree
units.guide:
The mitral valve prints 2 leaflets, 2 commissures, 1 annulus plus chordae tendineae, papillary muscles and adjacent LV myocardium (p346). MR is systolic retrograde LV→LA flow, a pure volume overload lesion with normal diastolic function.
Acute MR arises from papillary muscle rupture (inferior wall MI; posteromedial wall supplied only by RCA, m/c; infection) or chordae rupture (infective endocarditis); chronic MR splits into primary/organic (RHD m/c in developing, MVP m/c in developed, SLE/RA) and secondary/functional (annular abnormality, LV dysfunction m/c, annular dilatation with MR begets MR, HCM via SAM).

units.title: RHD Timeline and Combinations, Autoimmune Notes, and the Physiology-versus-Pathology Chains
units.sec: RHD Timeline and Combinations, Autoimmune Notes, and the Physiology-versus-Pathology Chains
units.guide:
Acute valvulitis at around 10 yrs leads after 15–20 yrs to RHD with MS+MR (m/c), MS+AR and AR+AS; m/c heart disease d/t RHD is MS while m/c rheumatic heart disease is MR (p347). Other autoimmune diseases are listed under the printed heading 'causing AR': Takayasu arteritis, Behcet's, ankylosing spondylitis.
Physiology runs S1 → isovolumetric contraction → AV valve open → rapid + reduced ejection → LV to aorta (high afterload). Pathology runs coaptation-zone failure (soft S1) → incompetence → LV→LA leak (LA gives ↓↓ afterload) → ↑ LA blood → ↑ LA→LV blood → eccentric hypertrophy with dilatation (↑ radius, thickness not increased) → eventual contractility impairment (severe MR) → LVF.

units.title: Laplace's Law, Afterload Reduction, the Severity Table, Normal EF and the Pulse/BP/Apex/JVP Findings
units.sec: Laplace's Law, Afterload Reduction, the Severity Table, Normal EF and the Pulse/BP/Apex/JVP Findings
units.guide:
Laplace: wall stress = pressure × radius/(2 × thickness); stress ∝ radius which keeps ↑ in MR till LVF; thin-walled LV needs less filling pressure (p348). NTG/sodium nitroprusside ↓ aortic afterload → more aortic flow, used in acute MR; strict BP control follows the same logic.
Severe/decompensated MR shows dyspnea +++ (LV failure), EF normal/↓↓ and ↑↑ LVEDP/LVESP against asymptomatic/palpitations, normal/↑↑ EF and normal pressures; normal EF in MR is 70% and <60% is bad prognosis needing treatment. Pseudocollapsing pulse keeps a well sustained peak and normal volume against collapsing's ill sustained peak and high volume (rapid up/downstroke shared); BP normal, severe MR → LV failure → narrow pulse pressure; apex down-out hyperkinetic; JVP v wave prominent in acute MR.

units.title: Soft S1 to S4, the Pansystolic Murmur Columns, Loudness Order, 60/40 Rule and MVP Features with the Venn Diagram
units.sec: Soft S1 to S4, the Pansystolic Murmur Columns, Loudness Order, 60/40 Rule and MVP Features with the Venn Diagram
units.guide:
Soft S1 follows loss of coaptation zone and ↓ dp/dt; severe MR gives early A2 (wide split S2); S3 is universal even without failure and S4 never occurs (p349). The pansystolic murmur reflects a whole-systole gradient, except acute MR's short decrescendo murmur; heard at apex, left lateral, breath held in expiration, diaphragm; high-frequency soft blowing without thrill, no respiratory variation; radiation axilla/back (jet backwards) or base (jet to interatrial septa); loudness ∝ gradient, MVP < RHD < LVD.
Treatment indications: symptomatic, or asymptomatic with EF ≤60%/LVESD ≥40 mm (60/40 rule); repair > replacement, and post-repair sudden ↑ afterload can cause LVF. MVP: redundant leaflet buckling into LA (floppy), posterior leaflet m/c, F > M 15–30 yrs, m/c asymptomatic; Venn A = myxomatous disease (pathology), B = MVP on ECHO, C–E in the hatched overlap.

units.title: MVP Complications Flowchart, NEC and Murmur Auscultation and Dynamic Auscultation with Cavity Size
units.sec: MVP Complications Flowchart, NEC and Murmur Auscultation and Dynamic Auscultation with Cavity Size
units.guide:
Excess leaflet tissue buckling into LA may carry GAG deposition: in annulus → weakening/dilatation/calcification → MR; in chordae → rupture → acute MR; pulling of chordae (papillary→LV myocardium) causes ischemic symptoms (palpitation, angina)/ectopics (p350). Auscultation: NEC and murmur, both or any one independently; murmur is high-pitched whooping (cooing dove), mid-systolic crescendo-decrescendo at apex, radiating to axilla (anterior leaflet) or aortic area (posterior leaflet).
Dynamic auscultation: Valsalva/sudden standing (↓ preload/↓ afterload) → ↓ ventricular blood → ↓ cavity → ↓ chordal stretch → more prolapse → click closer to S1 + longer murmur (figure ↓ impedance, ↑ contractility, ↓ volume); squatting/leg raising/standing-to-supine/isometric (↑ preload/↑ afterload) → ↑ cavity → more stretch → less prolapse → click away from S1 + shorter murmur (figure ↑ impedance, ↓ contractility, ↑ volume).

units.title: Brockenbrough Phenomenon, the MVP-versus-HCM Table and Acute MR Pathogenesis, Murmur and Treatment
units.sec: Brockenbrough Phenomenon, the MVP-versus-HCM Table and Acute MR Pathogenesis, Murmur and Treatment
units.guide:
Brockenbrough: post-VPC → compensatory pause → prolonged filling (↑ preload); in HCM ↑ force of contraction > ↑ preload → ↑ murmur intensity → ↑ gradient; in MVP cavity size stays normal so murmur is unchanged/↓ (p351). Table: standing/Valsalva ↑ duration (MVP) vs ↑ intensity (HCM); after VPC unchanged/↓ (MVP) vs ↑ intensity & duration (HCM).
Acute MR: rupture → non-compliant LA → ↑ LAP → ↑ PCWP → dyspnea (pulmonary edema); LV systolic function low/normal yet soon LVF → cardiogenic shock; short systolic decrescendo murmur; NTG/sodium nitroprusside till intervention, emergency CTVS surgery, bad prognosis.
